A common pathway is: vocational education in die making or CNC → workshop apprenticeship in turning, milling, and grinding → CNC programming and CAD/CAM → independent responsibility for complete dies → process design or die project management.

This work suits hands-on people who can concentrate and are highly sensitive to dimensions. If you can spend half a day investigating a one-millimeter deviation, the trade can provide long-term stability.

Tool and Die Makers design, manufacture, fit, and repair stamping dies, injection molds, die-casting dies, specialized tools, and fixtures. Their work includes reading drawings, machining, heat treatment, assembly, tryouts, and repair, making it one of manufacturing's most precision-intensive trades.

paragraphs: The routine cycle is drawings, process, machining, and verification. For a new die, first define the process route and fixturing plan. During machining, watch the toolpath continuously, then verify every tolerance with a micrometer. During assembly, use red-lead fitting to ensure closure accuracy. Finally, try out the die on an injection molding machine or press. The work is complete only when the product passes inspection.

In short: machine and assemble steel blanks into dies that mass-produce products. Duties include reading drawings and defining processes, operating turning, milling, grinding, and EDM equipment, programming and setting up machines, heat treatment, assembly and fitting, tryouts and repair, and maintaining measuring instruments and equipment.

Data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) show that about 55,200 tool and die makers were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to decline to 49,300 by 2034, a net decrease of about 5,900 jobs, with approximately 4,700 openings annually. Median annual pay in 2026 is about $63,200 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace tool and die makers, but it will clearly change how they work. Automated programming, simulation, and in-process inspection reduce trial-and-error costs. Software now calculates process parameters that experienced craftspeople once discovered through expensive experiments. What remains irreplaceable is process judgment: how materials deform under heat, where fitting surfaces need scraping, and whether a tryout defect comes from the cavity or gate. These abilities accumulate through decades of field experience.

Process planning: Comprehensive consideration of materials, machining allowance, fixturing, and heat-treatment sequence.

Balancing cost and schedule: Tradeoffs between precision requirements and machining cost.

paragraphs: A score of 5/10 means that half the work, including programming, measurement, and parameter recording, is being taken over by software and automation. This is an occupation with medium AI exposure.

Moderately high exposure does not mean half the jobs disappear. Workers limited to following programs face replacement, while process design and die-repair diagnosis gain importance. People who both program and repair dies are increasingly scarce at die shops, strengthening their bargaining power.

Do not feel embarrassed about studying die making or CNC at vocational school. This is one of the few trades that becomes more valuable with age. Master CAD/CAM and CNC programming in school, then spend two years learning from an experienced craftsperson. Your starting position will be well above that of a general assembly-line worker.

Address software gaps by learning automated programming, simulation, and in-process inspection. Advance from single-machine operation to process expertise, programming, and die repair, creating a stronger basis for negotiating pay.

A mechanical foundation makes entry easier. On your resume, specify the die types you built, tolerances achieved, and typical defects repaired. This is far more useful than stating that you can operate machine tools.

Do not recruit only experienced workers. Build a pipeline of apprentices working with senior craftspeople. Pay a premium for hybrid skills in programming + processes + die repair to preserve veteran craftsmanship.

subject.summary: Tool and die makers are the craftspeople of manufacturing. Injection molds for phone cases, cold-stamping dies for pressed parts, and cavities for die-cast parts all come from their machine tools and craftsmanship.
